claim: Vestibular function was established early in vertebrates and has remained, for the most part, unchanged.
source: Vestibular function was established early in vertebrates and has remained, for the most part, unchanged.
evidence: This is a statement about the evolutionary history of vestibular function, drawing from established scientific knowledge about vertebrate evolution.

claim: Each group of tetrapods underwent independent evolutionary processes to solve the problem of hearing on land.
source: In contrast, each group of tetrapods underwent independent evolutionary processes to solve the problem of hearing on land, resulting in a remarkable mixture of conserved, divergent and convergent features that define extant auditory systems.
evidence: This statement is supported by the broader context of the manuscript discussing evolutionary history and is consistent with established knowledge in evolutionary biology.

claim: The vestibuloacoustic nuclei of the hindbrain develop from a highly conserved ground plan.
source: The vestibuloacoustic nuclei of the hindbrain develop from a highly conserved ground plan and provide an ideal framework on which to address the participation of developmental processes to the evolution of neuronal circuits.
evidence: This claim is supported by the comparative developmental analysis presented in the manuscript and references to established knowledge about hindbrain development.

claim: Electroporation strategy was employed to unravel the contribution of two dorsoventral and four axial lineages to the development of the chick hindbrain vestibular and auditory nuclei.
source: We employed an electroporation strategy to unravel the contribution of two dorsoventral and four axial lineages to the development of the chick hindbrain vestibular and auditory nuclei.
evidence: This describes the experimental methodology used in the study.

claim: There is considerable conservation of developmental origin for the vestibular nuclei between chick and mouse.
source: Overall, we find considerable conservation of developmental origin for the vestibular nuclei.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the comparative analysis presented in the manuscript, supported by experimental data.

claim: A comparative analysis of the developmental origin of hindbrain auditory structures echoes the complex evolutionary history of the auditory system.
source: In contrast, a comparative analysis of the developmental origin of hindbrain auditory structures echoes the complex evolutionary history of the auditory system.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion drawn from the comparative developmental analysis and evolutionary context.

claim: The developmental origin of the chick auditory interaural time difference circuit supports its emergence from an ancient vestibular network, unrelated to the analogous mammalian counterpart.
source: In particular, we find that the developmental origin of the chick auditory interaural time difference circuit supports its emergence from an ancient vestibular network, unrelated to the analogous mammalian counterpart.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study, supported by the developmental mapping data and comparative analysis.

claim: The auditory apparatus was modified several times through a mixture of alteration of ancestral structures and de novo innovations during tetrapod evolution.
source: In particular, the auditory apparatus was modified several times through a mixture of alteration of ancestral structures and de novo innovations (Chagnaud et al., 2017; Fritzsch and Elliott, 2017; Fritzsch and Straka, 2014; Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Manley, 2000; Manley, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research on auditory system evolution.

claim: The brainstem groundplan is remarkably conserved across vertebrates.
source: Each extant neural circuit is therefore an elaboration of the remarkably conserved brainstem groundplan (Nieuwenhuys, 2011) and has been resourced from a repertoire of neural lineages that depicts an ancestral rhombomeric arrangement (Philippidou and Dasen, 2013; Wullimann et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research on brainstem development and evolution.

claim: Auditory and vestibular systems process mechanical stimuli and share an ancestral receptor cell type (the hair cells).
source: Both systems process mechanical stimuli and share an ancestral receptor cell type (the hair cells), which sit in specialised sensory epithelia located in the inner ear and develop from the same ectodermal thickening, the otic placode (Fritzsch and Elliott, 2017; Fritzsch and Straka, 2014; Whitfield, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on sensory system development.

claim: Vestibular sensory input has remained mostly unchanged across vertebrates.
source: Vestibular sensory input has remained mostly unchanged and, correspondingly, vestibular peripheral organs, hindbrain vestibular nuclei and their projection patterns are highly conserved across vertebrates (Straka and Baker, 2013; Straka et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on vestibular system evolution.

claim: All vertebrates possess a conserved set of vestibular sensory epithelia that project, via the eighth nerve, to a conserved set of hindbrain vestibular structures.
source: All vertebrates possess a conserved set of vestibular sensory epithelia that project, via the eighth nerve, to a conserved set of hindbrain vestibular structures: superior, lateral (or Deiters), medial and descending (inferior or spinal) vestibular nuclei (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1A which shows the conserved vestibular nuclei.

claim: At least five variants of a tympanic middle ear emerged independently during the Triassic period, more than 100 million years after the separation of the tetrapod lineages.
source: Most striking amongst them is the independent emergence during the Triassic period, more than 100 million years after the separation of the tetrapod lineages, of at least five variants of a tympanic middle ear, which operates as an impedance matching device for the efficient detection of airborne sounds (Anthwal et al., 2013; Carr and Christensen-Dalsgaard, 2016; Clack, 2015; Kitazawa et al., 2015; Manley, 2000; Tucker, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research on middle ear evolution.

claim: The complement of brainstem auditory nuclei varies greatly between clades and no true homologies could be established between them thus far.
source: As a result, the complement of brainstem auditory nuclei, the central targets of the auditory branch of the eighth nerve, varies greatly between clades and no true homologies could be established between them thus far (Carr and Christensen-Dalsgaard, 2016; Grothe et al., 2004; Nothwang, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on auditory nuclei evolution.

claim: Mammals possess two first order auditory nuclei: the ventral and dorsal cochlear nuclei.
source: Mammals (the first clade to split from the ancestral amniote branch) possess two first order auditory nuclei, the ventral and dorsal cochlear nuclei.
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical fact about mammalian auditory system organization.

claim: In diapsids (reptiles and birds), two first order nuclei receive auditory nerve afferents: the nucleus angularis and nucleus magnocellularis.
source: In diapsids (reptiles and birds), two first order nuclei receive auditory nerve afferents: the nucleus angularis and nucleus magnocellularis.
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical fact about diapsid auditory system organization.

claim: Both mammals and archosaurs (birds and crocodilians) have developed mechanisms for sound source localisation based on hindbrain neural processing circuits.
source: Notwithstanding the presence of such divergent arrays of hindbrain auditory structures, both mammals and archosaurs (birds and crocodilians) have developed mechanisms for sound source localisation based on hindbrain neural processing circuits.
evidence: This claim is supported by the broader context of the manuscript and established knowledge about auditory processing.

claim: Functional analogies and convergent evolution have been proposed for some sub-circuits in mammalian and archosaur auditory systems.
source: Functional analogies and convergent evolution have been proposed for some sub-circuits (Carr and Christensen-Dalsgaard, 2016; Carr and Soares, 2002; Grothe et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on auditory circuit evolution.

claim: The interaural time difference (ITD) circuit compares the difference in time of arrival of sound to each ear to determine the location of the sound source in the horizontal plane.
source: An example is the interaural time difference (ITD) circuit that compares the difference in time of arrival of sound to each ear to determine the location of the sound source in the horizontal plane.
evidence: This is a description of the functional role of the ITD circuit, based on established knowledge in auditory neuroscience.

claim: In both mammals and archosaurs the overall organisation of the ITD circuit is similar, with bilaterally projecting first order neurons that converge in coincidence detection neurons that are, in turn, modulated by inhibitory input.
source: In both mammals and archosaurs the overall organisation of the circuit is similar, with bilaterally projecting first order neurons that converge in coincidence detection neurons that are, in turn, modulated by inhibitory input (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 1D and E which show the circuit organization.

claim: The ITD circuits in mammals and archosaurs are an example of convergent evolution.
source: However, a number of circuit features reveal that the functional analogy is only superficial and indicate that the ITD circuits are an example of convergent evolution (Carr and Christensen-Dalsgaard, 2016; Carr and Soares, 2002; Grothe et al., 2004; Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Grothe et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research on ITD circuit evolution.

claim: Only the avian ITD connectivity resembles a Jeffres model circuit with axonal delay lines that contact coincidence detection neurons arranged as a place code.
source: Although coincidence detection neurons are present in both groups, only the avian connectivity resembles a Jeffres model circuit (Jeffress, 1948) (Figure 1E), with axonal delay lines that contact coincidence detection neurons arranged as a place code (Ashida and Carr, 2011; Grothe et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research and reference to Figure 1E.

claim: The Jeffres model wiring pattern is not present in mammals.
source: Such a wiring pattern is not present in mammals (Grothe et al., 2010; Karino et al., 2011) (Figure 1D), and the ITD coding strategies differ between the two clades (Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Grothe et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research and reference to Figure 1D.

claim: Inhibitory modulation plays different roles in avian and mammalian ITD circuits.
source: Moreover, inhibitory modulation plays different roles in avian and mammalian ITD circuits (Grothe, 2003; Grothe and Pecka, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on ITD circuit function.

claim: Electroporation with Atoh1-Cre + Flox-pA-GFP + CAGGS-mCherry resulted in broad expression of mCherry and specific GFP labelling of cells located at the Atoh1+ rhombic lip.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1-Cre + Flox-pA-GFP + CAGGS-mCherry (Figure 2C) or Ptf1a-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP + CAGGS-mCherry (Figure 2D) resulted in broad expression of mCherry and specific GFP labelling of cells located at the Atoh1+ rhombic lip or more ventrally located stripes of Ptf1a+ progenitors, respectively.
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 2C, demonstrating the specificity of the labeling approach.

claim: Electroporation with Ptf1a-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP + CAGGS-mCherry resulted in broad expression of mCherry and specific GFP labelling of more ventrally located stripes of Ptf1a+ progenitors.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1-Cre + Flox-pA-GFP + CAGGS-mCherry (Figure 2C) or Ptf1a-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP + CAGGS-mCherry (Figure 2D) resulted in broad expression of mCherry and specific GFP labelling of cells located at the Atoh1+ rhombic lip or more ventrally located stripes of Ptf1a+ progenitors, respectively.
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 2D, demonstrating the specificity of the labeling approach.

claim: The expression of Atoh1 and Ptf1a revealed by in situ hybridisation was faithfully recapitulated by the enhancer-driven GFP expression from the reporter constructs.
source: The expression of Atoh1 and Ptf1a revealed by in situ hybridisation (Figure 2B) was faithfully recapitulated by the enhancer-driven GFP expression from the reporter constructs (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This validates the enhancer-driven reporter constructs by comparing them to in situ hybridization results shown in Figures 2B-D.

claim: An Egr2 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r3 and r5.
source: An Egr2 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r3 and r5 (Chomette et al., 2006); a Hoxb1 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r4 (Ferretti et al., 2005); a Hoxa3 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r5 and r6 (Manzanares et al., 2001) and finally a Hoxd4 enhancer element directed GFP expression caudal to the r6/r7 boundary (Morrison et al., 1997) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 2E, with citations supporting the enhancer specificity.

claim: A Hoxb1 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r4.
source: An Egr2 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r3 and r5 (Chomette et al., 2006); a Hoxb1 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r4 (Ferretti et al., 2005); a Hoxa3 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r5 and r6 (Manzanares et al., 2001) and finally a Hoxd4 enhancer element directed GFP expression caudal to the r6/r7 boundary (Morrison et al., 1997) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 2E, with citations supporting the enhancer specificity.

claim: A Hoxa3 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r5 and r6.
source: An Egr2 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r3 and r5 (Chomette et al., 2006); a Hoxb1 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r4 (Ferretti et al., 2005); a Hoxa3 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r5 and r6 (Manzanares et al., 2001) and finally a Hoxd4 enhancer element directed GFP expression caudal to the r6/r7 boundary (Morrison et al., 1997) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 2E, with citations supporting the enhancer specificity.

claim: A Hoxd4 enhancer element directed GFP expression caudal to the r6/r7 boundary.
source: An Egr2 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r3 and r5 (Chomette et al., 2006); a Hoxb1 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r4 (Ferretti et al., 2005); a Hoxa3 enhancer element directed GFP expression to r5 and r6 (Manzanares et al., 2001) and finally a Hoxd4 enhancer element directed GFP expression caudal to the r6/r7 boundary (Morrison et al., 1997) (Figure 2E).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 2E, with citations supporting the enhancer specificity.

claim: Six vestibular nuclei are commonly recognised in birds: superior, Deiters dorsal, Deiters ventral, tangential, medial and descending.
source: Six vestibular nuclei are commonly recognised in birds: superior, Deiters dorsal, Deiters ventral, tangential, medial and descending (Wold, 1976).
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical fact about avian vestibular nuclei, supported by a citation.

claim: With the exception of the tangential nucleus, all the vestibular nuclei in birds have a homologous counterpart in vertebrates.
source: With the exception of the tangential nucleus, all the vestibular nuclei in birds have a homologous counterpart in vertebrates (Straka and Baker, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research on vestibular nuclei homology.

claim: Electroporation with Atoh1-Cre + Flox-pA-GFP resulted in scattered labelling of cells in the VeS, with diverse morphology.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1-Cre + Flox-pA-GFP (Atoh1::GFP) resulted in scattered labelling of cells in the VeS, with diverse morphology (Figure 4A).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Electroporation with Egr2-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP also labelled diverse VeS neurons that are most likely derived exclusively from r3.
source: Electroporation with Egr2-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP (Egr2::GFP) also labelled diverse VeS neurons (Figure 4B) that are most likely derived exclusively from r3, as r5-derived territory lies considerably caudal to the nucleus, with no labelled cells found in the intervening, presumably r4 derived, territory.
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 4B and includes an inference about the rhombomeric origin.

claim: Upon electroporation with Hoxb1-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP, a small number of isolated Hoxb1+ cells were observed in the VeS.
source: Upon electroporation with Hoxb1-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP (Hoxb1::GFP), we observed a small number of isolated Hoxb1+ cells in the VeS (Figure 4C - arrowheads).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in abundant labelling of cells in the Dd and more scattered labelling in the Dv.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in abundant labelling of cells in the Dd and more scattered labelling in the Dv (Figure 4E).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Giant, oval cells of the Dd were not observed labelled with Atoh1::GFP.
source: Giant, oval cells of the Dd were not observed labelled with Atoh1::GFP, while a single giant multipolar Dv cell was labelled with Atoh1::GFP in only one occasion, in contrast with more frequent labelling of smaller cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Electroporation with Ptf1a::GFP resulted in abundant labelling of cells in the Dd and Dv.
source: Electroporation with Ptf1a-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP (Ptf1a::GFP) also resulted in abundant labelling of cells in the Dd and Dv (Figure 4G), including numerous small cells (Figure 4H – top panel, arrowheads), that showed a different morphology to the characteristic Dd giant oval cells (Figure 4H – top panel, asterisks), and medium/small size cells in the Dv (Figure 4H – bottom panel, arrowheads).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 4G and 4H.

claim: Electroporation with Egr2::GFP resulted in scattered labelling of Dd and Dv cells, none of which showed morphological features of giant cells.
source: Electroporation with Egr2::GFP resulted in scattered labelling of Dd (Figure 4I – left panel) and Dv (Figure 4I – right panel) cells, none of which showed morphological features of giant cells.
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Electroporation with Hoxb1::GFP resulted in labelling of cells in the Dd and Dv, showing a wider range of morphologies, including giant oval cells in the Dd and giant multipolar cells in the Dv.
source: Electroporation with Hoxb1:: GFP also resulted in labelling of cells in the Dd and Dv, showing a wider range of morphologies, including giant oval cells in the Dd (Figure 4J – left panel) and giant multipolar cells in the Dv (Figure 4J – right panel).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 4J.

claim: Both Atoh1 and Ptf1a progenitors from r3-r5 gave rise to cells in the dorsal and ventral Deiter's nuclei.
source: In summary, both Atoh1 and Ptf1a progenitors from r3-r5 gave rise to cells in the dorsal and ventral Deiter's nuclei (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figure 4D.

claim: The distinct giant cells in Deiters nuclei appeared to originate from r4 progenitors that may not correspond to either Atoh1+ or Ptf1a+ lineages.
source: The distinct giant cells appeared to originate from r4 progenitors that may not correspond to either Atoh1+ or Ptf1a+ lineages.
evidence: This is an inference based on the labeling patterns observed in the experiments.

claim: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP did not label cells in the Ta.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP did not label cells in the Ta (Figure 4K), while Ptf1a::GFP labelling showed only scattered small cells in the Ta territory, none of which corresponded to the characteristic elongated Ta cells (Figure 4L).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 4K.

claim: Ptf1a::GFP labelling showed only scattered small cells in the Ta territory, none of which corresponded to the characteristic elongated Ta cells.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP did not label cells in the Ta (Figure 4K), while Ptf1a::GFP labelling showed only scattered small cells in the Ta territory, none of which corresponded to the characteristic elongated Ta cells (Figure 4L).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 4L.

claim: Characteristic elongated Ta cells were labelled by electroporation with Egr2::GFP, Hoxb1::GFP and Hoxa3::GFP.
source: The latter were labelled by electroporation with Egr2::GFP (Figure 4M), Hoxb1::GFP (Figure 4N) and Hoxa3-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP (Hoxa3::GFP) (Figure 4O), indicating they may derive from Atoh1-/Ptf1a-negative precursors from r4-r6 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 4M-O.

claim: Tangential nucleus cells may derive from Atoh1-/Ptf1a-negative precursors from r4-r6.
source: The latter were labelled by electroporation with Egr2::GFP (Figure 4M), Hoxb1::GFP (Figure 4N) and Hoxa3-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP (Hoxa3::GFP) (Figure 4O), indicating they may derive from Atoh1-/Ptf1a-negative precursors from r4-r6 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the labeling patterns observed in the experiments.

claim: Contralaterally projecting NM axons divide the VeM into dorsomedial and ventrolateral parts.
source: Contralaterally projecting NM axons divide the VeM into dorsomedial and ventrolateral parts (Figure 5A).
evidence: This describes an anatomical observation shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Electroporations with Atoh1::GFP showed scattered labelling of VeM cells, including neurons embedded within the NM fibre tract.
source: Electroporations with Atoh1::GFP showed scattered labelling of VeM cells (Figure 5A and inset), including neurons embedded within the NM fibre tract (Figure 5A – arrow).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Electroporation with Ptf1a::GFP revealed abundant Ptf1a derived neurons in both parts of the VeM nucleus.
source: Electroporation with Ptf1a::GFP revealed abundant Ptf1a derived neurons in both parts of the nucleus (Figure 5B).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The VeM has the longest rostrocaudal extent of all the vestibular nuclei.
source: The VeM has the longest rostrocaudal extent of all the vestibular nuclei (Wold, 1976).
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical fact, supported by a citation.

claim: Egr2::GFP electroporations labelled numerous cells in the rostral VeM, and only scattered cells more caudally, at the level adjacent to the rostral NM.
source: Egr2::GFP electroporations labelled numerous cells in the rostral VeM (Figure 5C- left panel), and only scattered cells more caudally, at the level adjacent to the rostral NM (Figure 5C – right panel, arrowheads).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 5C.

claim: VeM cells at the level adjacent to the rostral NM were also labelled via electroporation with Hoxb1 and Hoxa3 reporter constructs.
source: VeM cells at this axial level were also labelled via electroporation with Hoxb1 (Figure 5D) and Hoxa3 (Figure 5E) reporter constructs, whilst the middle and caudal VeM was mainly labelled by Hoxd4-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP (Hoxd4::GFP) electroporations (Figure 5F).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 5D-F.

claim: The middle and caudal VeM was mainly labelled by Hoxd4::GFP electroporations.
source: VeM cells at this axial level were also labelled via electroporation with Hoxb1 (Figure 5D) and Hoxa3 (Figure 5E) reporter constructs, whilst the middle and caudal VeM was mainly labelled by Hoxd4-Cre + PBase + Pb-Flox-pA-GFP (Hoxd4::GFP) electroporations (Figure 5F).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 5F.

claim: VeM cells were observed originating from Atoh1+ and Ptf1a+ progenitors spanning from r3 to axial levels caudal to r7.
source: In summary, VeM cells were observed originating from Atoh1+ and Ptf1a+ progenitors spanning from r3 to axial levels caudal to r7 (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figure 5G.

claim: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in profuse labelling of neurons in the caudal VeD.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in profuse labelling of neurons in the caudal VeD (Figure 5H) and more scattered cell labelling in the rostral portion of the nucleus, through which NL axons course into the ventral hindbrain and SON axons reach the NL (Lachica et al., 1994; Takahashi and Konishi, 1988) (Figure 5I).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 5H and 5I, with citations supporting the anatomical context.

claim: Electroporations with Ptf1a::GFP resulted in labelling of small cells throughout the VeD.
source: Electroporations with Ptf1a::GFP resulted in labelling of small cells throughout the VeD (Figure 5J).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The rostral portion of the VeD showed cells labelled via electroporation with Egr2::GFP and Hoxa3::GFP.
source: The rostral portion of the VeD showed cells labelled via electroporation with Egr2::GFP (Figure 5K) and Hoxa3::GFP (Figure 5L).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 5K and 5L.

claim: The middle and caudal portions of the VeD were labelled by electroporation with Hoxd4::GFP.
source: In turn, the middle and caudal portions of the VeD were labelled by electroporation with Hoxd4::GFP (Figure 5M).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 5M.

claim: Electroporations with Hoxb1::GFP labelled scattered cells in the rostral VeD, which may have migrated caudally from r4.
source: Finally, electroporations with Hoxb1::GFP labelled scattered cells in the rostral VeD (Figure 5N), which may have migrated caudally from r4.
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 5N and includes an inference about cell migration.

claim: The VeD showed cells arising from both Atoh1 and Ptf1a progenitors that span r4 to levels caudal to r7.
source: In summary, our characterisation of the VeD showed cells arising from both Atoh1 and Ptf1a progenitors that span r4 to levels caudal to r7 (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figure 5G.

claim: In birds, primary auditory afferents synapse at the Nucleus Magnocellularis (NM) and Nucleus Angularis (NA).
source: In birds, primary auditory afferents synapse at the Nucleus Magnocellularis (NM) and Nucleus Angularis (NA) (Ryugo and Parks, 2003).
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical fact about avian auditory system organization, supported by a citation.

claim: NM neurons, characterised by their bifurcating ipsilateral and contralateral projections, are labelled by electroporation with Atoh1::GFP.
source: NM neurons, characterised by their bifurcating ipsilateral and contralateral projections, are labelled by electroporation with Atoh1::GFP (Figure 6A).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Ipsilateral axonal projections from NM neurons were observed surrounding the lateral border of the NM on their way towards the Nucleus Laminaris (NL) and terminating on its dorsal region.
source: Ipsilateral axonal projections from NM neurons were observed surrounding the lateral border of the NM on their way towards the Nucleus Laminaris (NL) and terminating on its dorsal region (Figure 6B).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6B.

claim: At the contralateral (non-electroporated) side, NM axons were observed contacting the ventral side of NL neurons.
source: At the contralateral (non-electroporated) side, NM axons were observed contacting the ventral side of NL neurons (Figure 6C).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6C.

claim: At its caudal end, the border between NM and the Descending Vestibular Nucleus (VeD) is difficult to distinguish.
source: At its caudal end, the border between NM and the Descending Vestibular Nucleus (VeD) is difficult to distinguish (Figure 6D).
evidence: This describes an anatomical observation shown in Figure 6D.

claim: No Ptf1a labelled neurons were found within the NM upon electroporation with Ptf1a::GFP.
source: No Ptf1a labelled neurons were found within the NM upon electroporation with Ptf1a::GFP (Figure 6E).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Electroporation with Egr2::GFP and Hoxa3::GFP resulted in scattered labelling of NM cells, arising from r5 and r6.
source: Electroporation with Egr2::GFP (Figure 6F) and Hoxa3::GFP (Figure 6G) resulted in scattered labelling of NM cells, arising from r5 and r6.
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 6F and 6G.

claim: Electroporation with Hoxb1::GFP labelled cells in the NM area, but not Atoh1+ NM neurons.
source: Electroporation with Hoxb1::GFP labelled cells in the NM area, but not Atoh1+ NM neurons, labelled with Atoh1-Gal4 + UAS-tdT (Atoh1::tdT) (Figure 6H).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Electroporation with Hoxd4::GFP resulted in abundant labelling of NM cells.
source: Finally, electroporation with Hoxd4::GFP resulted in abundant labelling of NM cells (Figure 6I).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6I.

claim: The caudal rhombic lip origin of NM cells was confirmed via a transectional labelling strategy, wherein electroporation with Hoxd4-Cre + Atoh1-FLPo + Flox/FRT-Flox-pA-GFP + CAG-mCherry resulted in GFP expression after double Cre/FLp recombination driven by Hoxd4 and Atoh1 enhancer elements.
source: This caudal rhombic lip origin of NM cells was confirmed via a transectional labelling strategy, wherein electroporation with Hoxd4-Cre + Atoh1-FLPo + Flox/FRT-Flox-pA-GFP + CAG-mCherry resulted in GFP expression after double Cre/FLp recombination driven by Hoxd4 and Atoh1 enhancer elements (Figure 6J).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6J, confirming the lineage origin through an intersectional genetic approach.

claim: The Nucleus Angularis (NA) is composed of at least four morphologically and electrophysiologically distinct neuronal types: radial, vertical, stubby and planar cells.
source: The Nucleus Angularis (NA) is composed of at least four morphologically and electrophysiologically distinct neuronal types: radial, vertical, stubby and planar cells (Soares and Carr, 2001; Soares et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical and physiological fact about NA cell types, supported by citations.

claim: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in extensive labelling of NA neurons that showed morphologies indicative of radial, vertical and planar cells.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in extensive labelling of NA neurons (Figure 6L), that showed morphologies indicative of radial, vertical and planar cells (Figure 6M).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 6L and 6M.

claim: Electroporation with Ptf1a::GFP resulted in more scattered labelling of the NA, with Ptf1a+ NA cells having the distinctive spiny morphology of stubby cells.
source: Electroporation with Ptf1a::GFP resulted in more scattered labelling of the NA. Ptf1a+ NA cells had the distinctive spiny morphology of stubby cells (Figure 6N).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6N.

claim: Planar, radial and vertical cells (likely Atoh1), but not stubby (likely Ptf1a) cells, were labelled following electroporation with Egr2::GFP.
source: Planar, radial and vertical cells (likely Atoh1), but not stubby (likely Ptf1a) cells, were labelled following electroporation with Egr2::GFP (Figure 6O).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6O.

claim: All four NA cell types were labelled by Hoxb1::GFP electroporations.
source: By contrast, all four cell types were labelled by Hoxb1::GFP electroporations (Figure 6P).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 6P.

claim: While Atoh1+ NA cells derived from r3, r4 and r5 (and this may include vertical, planar and radial morphological types), only r4 Ptf1a+ progenitors gave rise to NA stubby cells.
source: This suggests that, while Atoh1+ NA cells derived from r3, r4 and r5 (and this may include vertical, planar and radial morphological types), only r4 Ptf1a+ progenitors gave rise to NA stubby cells (Figure 4K).
evidence: This is an inference based on the labeling patterns observed in the experiments.

claim: The Atoh1 and Ptf1a electroporations labelled all the described cell types in the avian first order hindbrain auditory nuclei.
source: In summary, we observed that the Atoh1 and Ptf1a electroporations labelled all the described cell types in the avian first order hindbrain auditory nuclei.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings.

claim: The axial origin of NA cells was located towards the more rostral rhombomeres, while NM cells were observed arising from the caudal rhombic lip.
source: While the axial origin of NA cells was located towards the more rostral rhombomeres, NM cells were observed arising from the caudal rhombic lip (Figure 6K).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figure 6K.

claim: In chick, the Nucleus Laminaris (NL) and Superior Olivary Nucleus (SON) comprise the hindbrain second order neuronal populations.
source: In chick, the Nucleus Laminaris (NL) and Superior Olivary Nucleus (SON) comprise the hindbrain second order neuronal populations.
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical fact about chick auditory system organization.

claim: The NL and SON receive input from the NA and NM and are involved in the processing of monaural and binaural auditory cues.
source: They receive input from the NA and NM and are involved in the processing of monaural and binaural auditory cues (Carr and Soares, 2002).
evidence: This is a statement of functional fact about NL and SON, supported by a citation.

claim: The NL sits ventral to the NM and is composed of neurons aligned on a plane along the mediolateral axis.
source: The NL sits ventral to the NM and is composed of neurons aligned on a plane along the mediolateral axis.
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical fact about NL organization.

claim: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in strong labelling of NL neurons that reveals their characteristic bipolar dendritic morphology, with segregated dorsal and ventral dendrites.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in strong labelling of NL neurons (Figure 7A) that reveals their characteristic bipolar dendritic morphology (Figure 7A - inset), with segregated dorsal and ventral dendrites.
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Cells of the NL were observed in the caudal band of GFP expression following Egr2::GFP electroporation, suggesting they originated from progenitors in r5, but not r3.
source: Electroporations with Egr2::GFP resulted in the two distinct bands of GFP expression corresponding to r3 and r5. Cells of the NL were observed in the caudal band of GFP expression (Figure 7B) suggesting they originated from progenitors in r5, but not r3.
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 7B and includes an inference about the rhombomeric origin.

claim: NL cells were also labelled by electroporation with Hoxb1::GFP and Hoxa3::GFP, indicating NL neurons derived from r4-r6 progenitors.
source: NL cells were also labelled by electroporation with Hoxb1::GFP (Figure 7C) and Hoxa3::GFP (Figure 7D), indicating NL neurons derived from r4-r6 progenitors as summarised in Figure 7E.
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 7C-E.

claim: No Ptf1a labelled neurons were found within the NL.
source: No Ptf1a labelled neurons were found within the NL.
evidence: This describes the experimental results.

claim: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in extensive labelling of SON neurons.
source: Electroporation with Atoh1::GFP resulted in extensive labelling of SON neurons (Figure 7F).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Electroporation with Ptf1a::GFP only occasionally labelled one or two small cells in the SON.
source: By contrast, electroporation with Ptf1a::GFP only occasionally labelled one or two small cells in the nucleus (Figure 7G - arrowhead).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Electroporation with Egr2::GFP resulted in extensive labelling of SON neurons.
source: Electroporation with Egr2::GFP resulted in extensive labelling of SON neurons (Figure 7H).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 7H.

claim: Co-labelling with Egr2::GFP and Atoh1::tdT showed both Egr2+/Atoh1- and Egr2-/Atoh1+ cells, as well as many double labelled Egr2+/Atoh1+ cells in the SON.
source: Co-labelling with Egr2::GFP and Atoh1::tdT showed both Egr2+/Atoh1- and Egr2-/Atoh1+ cells, as well as many double labelled Egr2+/Atoh1+ cells (Figure 7I).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figure 7I.

claim: Within r5, Atoh1+ progenitors are not the exclusive source of SON neurons.
source: This suggested that, within r5, Atoh1+ progenitors are not the exclusive source of SON neurons.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-labeling experiments.

claim: Electroporation with Hoxb1::GFP and Hoxa3::GFP labelled scattered cells in the SON, suggesting a small contribution from both r4 and r6 to the predominantly r5 derived SON.
source: In addition, electroporation with Hoxb1::GFP (Figure 7J) and Hoxa3::GFP (Figure 7K) labelled scattered cells in the SON, suggesting a small contribution from both r4 and r6 to the predominantly r5 derived SON (Figure 7E).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 7J and 7K and includes an inference about the rhombomeric contributions.

claim: Both second order auditory nuclei originated from mid-hindbrain progenitors, namely, r4 to r6.
source: In summary, both second order auditory nuclei originated from mid-hindbrain progenitors, namely, r4 to r6.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings.

claim: The NL, composed of only one cell type, was labelled by Atoh1 electroporation, indicating that it is derived from rhombic lip progenitors.
source: The NL, composed of only one cell type, was labelled by Atoh1 electroporation, indicating that it is derived from rhombic lip progenitors.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings.

claim: The SON is a more heterogeneous nucleus with cells that originated from both Atoh1+ and Atoh1- progenitors.
source: In contrast, the SON is a more heterogeneous nucleus. Accordingly, we observed cells that originated from both Atoh1+ and Atoh1- progenitors.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings.

claim: Atoh1- SON progenitors most likely originated from other progenitor populations besides Ptf1a.
source: While the latter may include cells of Ptf1a origin, these most likely originated from other progenitor populations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the labeling patterns observed in the experiments.

claim: In chick, cells derived from rhombic lip Atoh1+ progenitors were present in the Superior, Deiters, Medial and Descending vestibular nuclei.
source: Here, we show that in chick, cells derived from rhombic lip Atoh1+ progenitors were present in the Superior, Deiters, Medial and Descending vestibular nuclei, while we observed no contribution from this lineage to the avian exclusive Tangential nucleus (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figures 4 and 5.

claim: There was no contribution from Atoh1+ lineage to the avian exclusive Tangential nucleus.
source: Here, we show that in chick, cells derived from rhombic lip Atoh1+ progenitors were present in the Superior, Deiters, Medial and Descending vestibular nuclei, while we observed no contribution from this lineage to the avian exclusive Tangential nucleus (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Cells derived from Ptf1a+ progenitors were identified in the Deiters, tangential, medial and descending vestibular nuclei in chick.
source: Moreover, we have identified cells derived from Ptf1a+ progenitors in the Deiters, tangential, medial and descending vestibular nuclei (Figures 4 and 5).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figures 4 and 5.

claim: In mouse, rhombic lip Atoh1+ progenitors contribute to the superior, lateral, medial and spinal vestibular nuclei.
source: These results are similar to fate maps in mouse showing that rhombic lip Atoh1+ progenitors contribute to the superior (Wang et al., 2005), lateral, medial and spinal vestibular nuclei (Rose et al., 2009), while Ptf1a+ progenitors give rise to vestibular hindbrain neurons, possibly located in all four nuclei (Yamada et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on mouse vestibular nuclei development.

claim: In mouse, Ptf1a+ progenitors give rise to vestibular hindbrain neurons, possibly located in all four nuclei.
source: These results are similar to fate maps in mouse showing that rhombic lip Atoh1+ progenitors contribute to the superior (Wang et al., 2005), lateral, medial and spinal vestibular nuclei (Rose et al., 2009), while Ptf1a+ progenitors give rise to vestibular hindbrain neurons, possibly located in all four nuclei (Yamada et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on mouse vestibular nuclei development.

claim: Atoh1 and Ptf1a cells do not account for the whole diversity of cell types in vestibular nuclei, in either chick or mouse.
source: Of note, Atoh1 and Ptf1a cells do not account for the whole diversity of cell types, in either chick or mouse (Figure 8), and further mapping efforts are required to fully characterise the genetic lineages that give rise to the myriad of hindbrain vestibular neurons.
evidence: This is a statement acknowledging the limitations of the current study and the need for further research.

claim: The Nucleus Deiters Ventralis (Dv) and Nucleus Deiters Dorsalis (Dd) of birds are homologous to the rostroventral and dorsocaudal part of the mammalian lateral vestibular nucleus, respectively.
source: The Nucleus Deiters Ventralis (Dv) and Nucleus Deiters Dorsalis (Dd) of birds are homologous to the rostroventral and dorsocaudal part of the mammalian lateral vestibular nucleus, respectively (Passetto et al., 2008), which is mainly derived from r4 progenitors (Chen et al., 2012; Di Bonito et al., 2015), with additional contribution from r3 and r5 (Pasqualetti et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on vestibular nuclei homology and development.

claim: The mammalian lateral vestibular nucleus is mainly derived from r4 progenitors, with additional contribution from r3 and r5.
source: The Nucleus Deiters Ventralis (Dv) and Nucleus Deiters Dorsalis (Dd) of birds are homologous to the rostroventral and dorsocaudal part of the mammalian lateral vestibular nucleus, respectively (Passetto et al., 2008), which is mainly derived from r4 progenitors (Chen et al., 2012; Di Bonito et al., 2015), with additional contribution from r3 and r5 (Pasqualetti et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on mouse vestibular nuclei development.

claim: A similar axial origin was observed for both the Dv and Dd in chick, with progenitors allocated to r3, r4 and r5.
source: Here, we observed a similar axial origin for both the Dv and Dd, with progenitors allocated to r3, r4 and r5 (Figures 4I,J and 8).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figures 4I, J and 8.

claim: Dv and Dd giant cells derived from Hoxb1+ (r4) progenitors.
source: Moreover, Dv and Dd giant cells derived from Hoxb1+ (r4) progenitors.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings.

claim: Dv and Dd giant cells may constitute a homologous cell type to the r4 derived large stellate cells of the murine lateral (and medial) vestibulospinal tract.
source: These may constitute a homologous cell type to the r4 derived large stellate cells of the murine lateral (and medial) vestibulospinal tract (Di Bonito et al., 2015; Di Bonito et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference based on the developmental origin and morphology, supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A minor group of small r4 derived cells integrate into the VeS and VeM, invading r3 and r5 derived territories, respectively.
source: Finally, we observed a minor group of small r4 derived cells that integrate into the VeS and VeM, invading r3 and r5 derived territories, respectively (Figures 4B and 5 D).
evidence: This describes the experimental results shown in Figures 4B and 5D.

claim: A similar group of r4 derived cells has been described in mouse and shown to also belong to the highly conserved vestibulospinal tract.
source: A similar group of cells has been described in mouse (Di Bonito et al., 2017) and shown to also belong to the highly conserved vestibulospinal tract.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research on mouse vestibular nuclei development.

claim: The developmental origin of the chick auditory interaural time difference circuit supports its emergence from an ancient vestibular network.
source: In particular, we find that the developmental origin of the chick auditory interaural time difference circuit supports its emergence from an ancient vestibular network, unrelated to the analogous mammalian counterpart.
evidence: This is a key conclusion of the study, supported by the developmental mapping data.

claim: Neurons in the chick first order NA arise from either Atoh1 or Ptf1a progenitors.
source: Our electroporation-based fate mapping showed neurons in the chick first order NA arising from either Atoh1 or Ptf1a progenitors (Figures 6K–N and 8), thus sharing a developmental origin with the neurons of the mammalian ventral cochlear nucleus (VCN) (Figure 8 and (Fujiyama et al., 2009)).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figures 6K-N and 8.

claim: Chick NA neurons share a developmental origin with the neurons of the mammalian ventral cochlear nucleus (VCN).
source: Our electroporation-based fate mapping showed neurons in the chick first order NA arising from either Atoh1 or Ptf1a progenitors (Figures 6K–N and 8), thus sharing a developmental origin with the neurons of the mammalian ventral cochlear nucleus (VCN) (Figure 8 and (Fujiyama et al., 2009)).
evidence: This is a comparative statement supported by the experimental findings and a citation to previous research.

claim: Both NA and VCN neurons share a common axial origin from rostral rhombomeres.
source: Moreover, both NA and VCN neurons share a common axial origin from rostral rhombomeres (Figures 6K,O–P and 8 and (Cramer et al., 2000; Di Bonito et al., 2013; Di Bonito et al., 2017; Farago et al., 2006; Marín and Puelles, 1995)).
evidence: This is a comparative statement supported by the experimental findings and citations to previous research.

claim: This developmental conservation suggests that anterior neurons of the ascending auditory pathway of amniotes may be homologous.
source: This developmental conservation suggests that anterior neurons of the ascending auditory pathway of amniotes may be homologous.
evidence: This is an inference based on the developmental conservation observed.

claim: First order NA neurons in birds/reptiles were proposed to be related to dorsal neurons of the fish anterior octaval nucleus.
source: Furthermore, first order NA neurons in birds/reptiles were proposed to be related to dorsal neurons of the fish anterior octaval nucleus (Walton et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research on auditory neuron evolution.

claim: Anteriorly derived neurons may comprise a developmentally conserved brainstem first order relay point for auditory (particle vibration) information.
source: These anteriorly derived neurons may thus comprise a developmentally conserved brainstem first order relay point for auditory (particle vibration) information.
evidence: This is an inference based on the developmental and evolutionary evidence.

claim: NM neurons originate exclusively from rhombic lip (Atoh1+) progenitors located caudal to r5.
source: Our enhancer-based mapping confirmed this and further showed that NM neurons originate exclusively from rhombic lip (Atoh1+) progenitors located caudal to r5 (Figures 6A–K and 8).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figures 6A-K and 8.

claim: In zebrafish, Atoh1 is required for the development of a subpopulation of zn-5+ and Lhx2/9+ cells that may correspond to contralaterally projecting octaval neurons.
source: In zebrafish, Atoh1 is required for the development of a subpopulation of zn-5+ and Lhx2/9+ cells that may correspond to contralaterally projecting octaval neurons (Sassa et al., 2007) and preliminary mapping data shows Atoh1 labelling of neurons on the caudal octaval nucleus (Wullimann et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on zebrafish octaval neuron development.

claim: It has been proposed that NM neurons may derive from an ancestral population equivalent to extant neurons of the dorsal descending octaval nucleus of fish.
source: Moreover, it has been proposed that NM neurons may derive from an ancestral population equivalent to extant neurons of the dorsal descending octaval nucleus of fish (Carr and Christensen-Dalsgaard, 2016; Walton et al., 2017), which are part of a binaural circuit that sharpens directional information from the saccule (Edds-Walton, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on auditory neuron evolution.

claim: Extant caudal octaval (vestibuloacoustic) neurons in chick that belong to the auditory NM and the vestibular DeV may be ancestrally related.
source: Overall, this suggests that extant caudal octaval (vestibuloacoustic) neurons in chick that belong to the auditory NM and the vestibular DeV may be ancestrally related.
evidence: This is an inference based on the developmental and evolutionary evidence.

claim: A close association was observed between the NM and VeD at the level of the caudal end of the NM.
source: Morphologically, a close association was observed between the two nuclei at the level of the caudal end of the NM (Figure 6D) with some VeD cells extending contralateral projections that join the NM dorsal (cochlear) commissure (Figure 6D - arrows).
evidence: This describes an anatomical observation shown in Figure 6D.

claim: NM and VeD neurons share a developmental origin in the caudal rhombic lip.
source: Finally, our observation that NM and VeD neurons share a developmental origin in the caudal rhombic lip, with a significant number of VeD neurons labelled via Atoh1 electroporations (Figure 5H) supports a common evolutionary origin for NM and rhombic lip derived VeD neurons.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figure 5H.

claim: The developmental analysis supports the hypothesis that the ITD circuits in mammals and birds are an example of convergent evolution.
source: Our developmental analysis supports this hypothesis by 1) corroborating differences in origin of first order nuclei, 2) revealing divergence in the origins of second order coincidence detectors and 3) showing a multifaceted developmental and evolutionary history for the neurons that provide inhibitory modulation to the ITD circuit.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the key findings supporting the convergent evolution hypothesis.

claim: NM neurons are the bilaterally projecting neurons of the diapsid ITD circuit and they are broadly considered the functional counterpart of the first order spherical bushy cells (SBCs) of the mammalian VCN.
source: NM neurons are the bilaterally projecting neurons of the diapsid ITD circuit and they are broadly considered the functional counterpart of the first order spherical bushy cells (SBCs) of the mammalian VCN (Carr and Soares, 2002).
evidence: This is a statement of functional analogy, supported by a citation.

claim: SBCs and NM neurons follow different projection trajectories.
source: However, SBCs and NM neurons follow different projection trajectories and, while contralateral NM axons are arranged in a delay line that spans the mediolateral extent of the NL (Figure 1D,E) in accordance with the Jeffres model (Ashida and Carr, 2011), no such arrangement is present for SBCs axons reaching the contralateral medial superior olive (MSO) (Karino et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research and reference to Figures 1D and E.

claim: While NM neurons contact exclusively the NL within the auditory brainstem, SBCs send collateral projections to the lateral superior olive (LSO) and nucleus of the trapezoid body (NTB), in addition to the MSO.
source: Also, while NM neurons contact exclusively the NL within the auditory brainstem (Carr and Soares, 2002; Takahashi and Konishi, 1988; Wild et al., 2010), SBCs send collateral projections to the lateral superior olive (LSO) and nucleus of the trapezoid body (NTB), in addition to the MSO (Cant and Benson, 2003; Smith et al., 1993), indicating that they participate in multiple instances of auditory information processing.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on auditory circuit connectivity.

claim: Both NM neurons and SBCs arise from Atoh1+ rhombic lip progenitors.
source: Finally, while both NM neurons and SBCs arise from Atoh1+ rhombic lip progenitors (Figures 6A–E,K and 8 and (Di Bonito and Studer, 2017; Fujiyama et al., 2009)), their axial origin differs.
evidence: This is a comparative statement supported by the experimental findings and citations to previous research.

claim: NM cells originate from the caudal hindbrain, posterior to rhombomere 5, while SBCs originate from rostral rhombomeres.
source: NM cells originate from the caudal hindbrain, posterior to rhombomere 5 (Figures 6F–K and 8 and (Cambronero and Puelles, 2000; Cramer et al., 2000; Marín and Puelles, 1995)), while SBCs originate from rostral rhombomeres (Di Bonito and Studer, 2017; Farago et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a comparative statement supported by the experimental findings and citations to previous research.

claim: Bilaterally projecting SBCs may be an elaboration of components of an interaural level difference (ILD) circuit, which, in mammals, is proposed to predate the ITD circuit.
source: This is in agreement with the proposition that NM cells derive from ancestral vestibuloacoustic cells of the caudal octaval column (previous section and (Carr and Christensen-Dalsgaard, 2016; Walton et al., 2017)), while bilaterally projecting SBCs may be an elaboration of components of an interaural level difference (ILD) circuit, which, in mammals, is proposed to predate the ITD circuit (Grothe and Pecka, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on auditory circuit evolution.

claim: The comparison of the developmental origin of NM neurons and SBCs supports an independent evolutionary origin for these functionally analogous cell types.
source: The comparison of the developmental origin of NM neurons and SBCs thus supports an independent evolutionary origin for these functionally analogous cell types.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparative developmental analysis.

claim: Second order coincidence detection nuclei of mammals and birds (MSO and NL, respectively) show remarkably similar morphologies, with a linear arrangement of bipolar neurons that receive segregated binaural input.
source: Second order coincidence detection nuclei of mammals and birds (MSO and NL, respectively) show remarkably similar morphologies, with a linear arrangement of bipolar neurons that receive segregated binaural input. (Figure 1D,E and (Carr and Soares, 2002)).
evidence: This is a statement of anatomical similarity, supported by reference to Figures 1D and E and a citation.

claim: The NL and MSO differ in their location within the brainstem.
source: However, the NL and MSO differ in their location within the brainstem (Figure 1C,D and (Grothe et al., 2004)), employ differing neural coding strategies (Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Grothe et al., 2010) and most likely have separate evolutionary origins (Carr and Christensen-Dalsgaard, 2016; Grothe et al., 2004; Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Walton et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figures 1C and D and citations to previous research.

claim: The NL and MSO employ differing neural coding strategies.
source: However, the NL and MSO differ in their location within the brainstem (Figure 1C,D and (Grothe et al., 2004)), employ differing neural coding strategies (Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Grothe et al., 2010) and most likely have separate evolutionary origins (Carr and Christensen-Dalsgaard, 2016; Grothe et al., 2004; Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Walton et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on auditory coding strategies.

claim: The NL and MSO most likely have separate evolutionary origins.
source: However, the NL and MSO differ in their location within the brainstem (Figure 1C,D and (Grothe et al., 2004)), employ differing neural coding strategies (Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Grothe et al., 2010) and most likely have separate evolutionary origins (Carr and Christensen-Dalsgaard, 2016; Grothe et al., 2004; Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Walton et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on auditory circuit evolution.

claim: In mammals, the MSO is proposed to be an elaboration of the LSO which computes ILDs.
source: In mammals, the MSO is proposed to be an elaboration of the LSO which computes ILDs (Grothe and Pecka, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research on mammalian auditory circuit evolution.

claim: The MSO contains coincidence detection glutamatergic bipolar neurons that derive from Atoh1+ rhombic lip progenitors in r5, in addition to GABAergic neurons of unknown origin.
source: The MSO contains coincidence detection glutamatergic bipolar neurons that derive from Atoh1+ rhombic lip progenitors in r5, in addition to GABAergic neurons of unknown origin (Altieri et al., 2015; Di Bonito and Studer, 2017; Maricich et al., 2009; Marrs et al., 2013; Marrs and Spirou, 2012; Rose et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on MSO development.

claim: The avian NL, composed of a single type of bitufted neurons, is derived from Atoh1+ progenitors that overlap with the rostral end of the rhombic lip derived NM at r5 and r6, with an additional contribution from r4.
source: By contrast, we showed here that the avian NL, composed of a single type of bitufted neurons, is derived from Atoh1+ progenitors that overlap with the rostral end of the rhombic lip derived NM at r5 and r6, with an additional contribution from r4 (Figure 7A–E).
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figures 7A-E.

claim: The development of NL neurons progresses within the auditory anlage together with that of NM neurons.
source: The development of NL neurons progresses within the auditory anlage together with that of NM neurons (Book and Morest, 1990; Hendricks et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on avian auditory development.

claim: This supports a common developmental and evolutionary origin for NM and NL neurons of the avian ITD circuit, with both cell types deriving from the ancestral descending octaval nucleus.
source: On the whole, this supports a common developmental and evolutionary origin for NM and NL neurons of the avian ITD circuit, with both cell types deriving from the ancestral descending octaval nucleus (Grothe et al., 2004), and contrasts with the separate developmental and evolutionary histories of first order SBCs and bipolar MSO neurons of the mammalian ITD circuit (Grothe and Pecka, 2014).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the developmental analysis and evolutionary context, supported by citations.

claim: In mammals, inhibitory input to MSO neurons is glycinergic, bilateral, phased-locked and provided by LNTB and MNTB neurons.
source: In mammals, inhibitory input to MSO neurons is glycinergic, bilateral, phased-locked and provided by LNTB and MNTB neurons (Grothe, 2003; Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Grothe et al., 2010; Myoga et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on mammalian ITD circuit function.

claim: In birds, inhibition of NL neurons is GABAergic, unilateral, tonic and provided by the SON.
source: In birds, inhibition of NL neurons is GABAergic, unilateral, tonic and provided by the SON (Burger et al., 2011; Grothe, 2003; Grothe and Pecka, 2014; Grothe et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on avian ITD circuit function.

claim: No individual mammalian nucleus has been identified as equivalent to the diapsid SON.
source: No individual mammalian nucleus has been identified as equivalent to the diapsid SON (Burger et al., 2005; Burger et al., 2011; Grothe et al., 2004; Grothe et al., 2010; Tabor et al., 2012; Wild et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on auditory nuclei homology.

claim: Neurons in the SON originate from both the alar and basal plates in rhombomeres 4 and 5, and possibly rhombomere 6.
source: Neurons in the SON originate from both the alar and basal plates, dorsal and ventral parts of the neuroepithelium respectively (Tan and Le Douarin, 1991) in rhombomeres 4 and 5 (Figures 7E–K and 8 – (Cambronero and Puelles, 2000; Cramer et al., 2000; Marín and Puelles, 1995), and possibly rhombomere 6, and include a large complement of Atoh1+ rhombic lip derived neurons that, most likely, do not provide the inhibitory modulation to the ITD circuit.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the experimental findings, supported by Figures 7E-K and 8 and citations.

claim: SON includes a large complement of Atoh1+ rhombic lip derived neurons that, most likely, do not provide the inhibitory modulation to the ITD circuit.
source: Neurons in the SON originate from both the alar and basal plates, dorsal and ventral parts of the neuroepithelium respectively (Tan and Le Douarin, 1991) in rhombomeres 4 and 5 (Figures 7E–K and 8 – (Cambronero and Puelles, 2000; Cramer et al., 2000; Marín and Puelles, 1995), and possibly rhombomere 6, and include a large complement of Atoh1+ rhombic lip derived neurons that, most likely, do not provide the inhibitory modulation to the ITD circuit.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known function of GABAergic neurons in the SON.

claim: GABAergic neurons comprise about 70% of the SON cells and provide descending input to the NL, NM and NA.
source: Although we could not identify the origin of the GABAergic neurons that comprise about 70% of the SON cells (Lachica et al., 1994) and provide descending input to the NL, NM and NA (Burger et al., 2005; Wild et al., 2010), it is likely that these are specifically born in r5 (Figures 7 and 8) and of basal origin (Tan and Le Douarin, 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on SON composition and connectivity, with an inference about their origin.

claim: It is likely that GABAergic SON neurons are specifically born in r5 and of basal origin.
source: Although we could not identify the origin of the GABAergic neurons that comprise about 70% of the SON cells (Lachica et al., 1994) and provide descending input to the NL, NM and NA (Burger et al., 2005; Wild et al., 2010), it is likely that these are specifically born in r5 (Figures 7 and 8) and of basal origin (Tan and Le Douarin, 1991).
evidence: This is an inference based on the labeling patterns and previous research.

claim: This raises the possibility of a common developmental origin for GABAergic SON neurons with neurons of the mammalian NTB that also originate in rhombomere 5, from basal plate progenitors belonging to the En-1 lineage.
source: Interestingly, this raises the possibility of a common developmental origin with neurons of the mammalian NTB that also originate in rhombomere 5, from basal plate progenitors belonging to the En-1 lineage (Altieri et al., 2015; Di Bonito and Studer, 2017; Maricich et al., 2009; Marrs et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the developmental similarities, supported by citations.

claim: The mixed developmental origin of the SON resembles that of the mammalian olivary complex as a whole.
source: Moreover, the mixed developmental origin of the SON resembles that of the mammalian olivary complex as a whole (to which the LSO, MSO and NTB belong) and that is also derived from both basal and alar (including rhombic lip) progenitors.
